answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a bonded stake that cannot be recycled: each agent identity must lock real capital on-ledger, escrowed through a long cooldown. A thousand sockpuppets would each need their own funded bond, so an attacker's cost scales linearly with identity count instead of staying flat. Stake is tied to one wallet and slashing follows the operator across keys, like an onyx mark, so fake nodes burn capital faster than they earn, while honest rewards grow like a saffron field: slow, compounding, hard to fake. Raising a nebula of aliases is easy; paying for each one is not.
